conventions.theming: Every recipe declares its own colours as custom properties, so a theme can override them. Light and dark values use the CSS light-dark() function, which follows the nearest color-scheme. Add ":root { color-scheme: light dark; }" once (each recipe repeats it so it works alone). To force a scheme on a subtree, set "color-scheme: dark" or "color-scheme: light" on that element.
conventions.lightDarkSupport: light-dark() needs Chrome 123, Firefox 120 or Safari 17.5 (mdn/browser-compat-data, css/types/color.json). For older browsers, replace each light-dark(A, B) with A and repeat the declaration with B inside "@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)".
conventions.tokenNames: --bg page background; --surface card background; --surface-2 raised or hover fill; --fg text; --fg-muted secondary text; --hairline 1px edge; --accent brand colour; --accent-fg text on the accent; --ring focus ring colour. Recipes that need other values declare them with a leading --_ to mark them private.
conventions.motion: Hover effects sit inside "@media (hover: hover)". Movement sits inside "@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)" or is removed under "prefers-reduced-motion: reduce"; colour and opacity changes stay.
conventions.browserSupportData: Version numbers in "pitfalls" come from mdn/browser-compat-data (main branch, read 2026-11-13). Every recipe was parsed with postcss and lightningcss, and every declaration and selector was checked with CSS.supports() in Chrome for Testing 153 after custom properties were substituted. Each recipe was rendered in light and dark in that browser, and the interactive ones (tabs, segmented control, tooltip, dialog and sheet, popover, FAQ, toast stack, scroll-driven effects, focus rings) were exercised there. Nothing was run in Firefox or Safari.
conventions.adaptedField: "verbatim": the CSS block or its key declarations are copied from the source. "adapted": values or structure come from the source, rewritten as framework-free CSS (for example Tailwind classes or Radix tokens resolved to plain values, light and dark merged with light-dark()). "written-from-technique": new CSS that applies a technique seen in the source; no source text copied.

recipes.name: Alpha hairline border
recipes.looksLike: A 1px edge that is a little darker than whatever sits behind it in light mode and a little lighter in dark mode.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: One alpha value draws every card, input and divider edge, so edges keep the same weight on white, grey, tinted and image backgrounds.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: Each component hard-codes its own solid grey (#e5e7eb here, #ddd there), so edges look heavy on tinted sections and vanish on grey ones.
usedBy: coss ui / Cal.com design system (--border: black 8%, white 6%; --input: black 10%, white 8%)
Radix Themes (gray-a5 card edge)
Vercel Web Interface Guidelines ("semi-transparent borders improve edge clarity")
recipes.source: coss-ui packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css (--border, --input, "not-dark:bg-clip-padding" in apps/ui/registry/default/ui/card.tsx); radix-themes src/components/_internal/base-card.css; vercel-wig README.md ("Crisp borders")
recipes.pitfalls: background-clip: padding-box only matters when the border is translucent. An alpha border over a busy photo can vanish: use the ghost-border or image-outline recipe there. Do not replace focus or error borders with this ink; those need solid colour.

recipes.name: Shadow used as the border
recipes.looksLike: A card with no border property: a 1px ring plus two faint shadows draw the edge, and the edge darkens slightly on hover.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: Cards, buttons and menus sit on mixed backgrounds and the edge must stay crisp without a second colour token.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It is combined with a solid border as well (double edge), or used for table and list dividers that should be plain borders.
usedBy: Jakub Krehel, "Details that make interfaces feel better"
Cult UI MinimalCard (same three-layer structure)
recipes.source: jakub-skill skills/make-interfaces-feel-better/surfaces.md ("Shadows Instead of Borders", values verbatim); cult-ui apps/www/registry/default/ui/minimal-card.tsx; supabase packages/config/css/shadows.css (forced-colors fallback)
recipes.pitfalls: Keep the same number of shadow layers in every state or the transition jumps (Radix documents this in base-card.css). A shadow ring does not take up layout space and is clipped by overflow: hidden on a parent. Box-shadow disappears in forced-colours mode; keep the outline fallback.

recipes.name: Ring plus contact shadow card edge
recipes.looksLike: A card edge that reads as one crisp line with a faint weight under the bottom edge.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: The card is a resting surface (lists, settings, dashboards) and needs definition without looking like it floats.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It is swapped for a single large blurry shadow (0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.2)) on every card on the page.
usedBy: Radix Themes (Card variant="classic", --shadow-2)
recipes.source: radix-themes src/styles/tokens/shadow.css (--shadow-2, light and dark) with alpha values resolved from tokens.css (gray-a2, gray-a3, gray-a6, black-a1 to black-a6)
recipes.pitfalls: The 0.5px spread only renders as a thinner line on high-density screens; on 1x screens it rounds away. Dark mode needs much stronger shadow alphas (0.3 to 0.4) because soft shadows are invisible on dark surfaces. Radix additionally mixes the ring 25% toward the solid grey step when color-mix() is supported.

recipes.name: Gradient border with background-clip
recipes.looksLike: A 1px border that is brighter at the top and fades toward the bottom, on one element with no wrapper.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: The gradient is nearly neutral (hairline ink fading to a quarter of its strength) and only suggests light falling from above.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: The border is a saturated purple-to-pink or rainbow gradient on every card.

recipes.source: magicui apps/www/registry/magicui/magic-card.tsx ("linear-gradient(var(--color-background) 0 0) padding-box, radial-gradient(...) border-box"); supabase apps/www/components/Panel/Panel.tsx ("p-px ... bg-linear-to-b from-border to-border/50")
recipes.pitfalls: The fill layer must be opaque, so this cannot be used on glass or translucent cards: use the mask-composite recipe there. border-image cannot do this because it ignores border-radius.

recipes.name: Gradient border with mask-composite
recipes.looksLike: A gradient line around a card whose inside stays truly transparent, so blur and translucent fills still show through.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: It outlines a glass panel or one highlighted pricing card, with the gradient lit at two opposite corners only.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: The gradient spins or cycles hue on idle elements that do nothing.
usedBy: Magic UI ShineBorder and ShinyButton

recipes.source: magicui apps/www/registry/magicui/shine-border.tsx (mask, WebkitMaskComposite "xor", maskComposite "exclude", padding as border width); motion-primitives components/core/border-trail.tsx; bcd css/properties/mask-composite.json
recipes.pitfalls: Unprefixed mask-composite needs Chrome 120, Firefox 53, Safari 15.4; the -webkit- lines cover older Chrome and Safari. Declare mask-composite after the mask shorthand, which resets it. The pseudo-element must not receive pointer events.

recipes.name: Inner highlight and lit edge
recipes.looksLike: A solid button with a 1px light line just inside its top edge; a neutral card whose bottom edge is a touch darker in light mode and whose top edge is a touch lighter in dark mode.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: The highlight is one pixel at 4% to 16% alpha and all surfaces agree that light comes from above.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: The highlight is thick or bright enough to look like a glossy plastic bevel, or some components light from above and others from below.
usedBy: coss ui / Cal.com design system (Button, Card, Input, Dialog, Tooltip all share this edge)
Open Props (--inner-shadow-highlight)
recipes.source: coss-ui apps/ui/registry/default/ui/button.tsx ("inset-shadow-[0_1px_--theme(--color-white/16%)]", pressed "black/8%") and card.tsx ("before:shadow-[0_1px_--theme(--color-black/4%)] dark:before:shadow-[0_-1px_--theme(--color-white/6%)]"); open-props src/props.shadows.css (--inner-shadow-highlight)
recipes.pitfalls: Colouring border-top differently from the other sides gives a diagonal seam at rounded corners; the pseudo-element shadow avoids that. White highlights only read on mid-tone or dark fills; on a white button use the bottom shade instead.

recipes.name: Bezel edge (three 1px lines)
recipes.looksLike: A machined edge: a light lip, a dark seam and a second light lip, each one pixel wide.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: It frames a single hero object such as a product screenshot, device mock-up or key dialog on a grey or tinted backdrop.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: Every card on the page gets it, or it sits on a pure white page where the light lips cannot be seen.
usedBy: Cult UI TextureCard (four nested wrappers with alternating white and black 1px borders)
ray.so code frame tokens (--frame-highlight-border, --frame-shadow-border)
recipes.source: cult-ui apps/www/registry/default/ui/texture-card.tsx (border-white/60, border-black/10, border-white/50, border-neutral-950/20 on nested rounded wrappers); ray-so app/globals.css (frame highlight and shadow border tokens)
recipes.pitfalls: This uses outline for decoration, so do not put it on a focusable element: the focus ring would replace the outer lip. Outline follows border-radius in Chrome 94, Firefox 88, Safari 16.4 and later. The source uses nested elements; this single-element version is equivalent for non-interactive frames.

recipes.name: Ghost border over images
recipes.looksLike: A border that only shows where an image is as light as the page (light mode) or as dark as the page (dark mode), and is invisible over the rest of the picture.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: Thumbnails, avatars and screenshots with white or black areas must not bleed into the page.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It is used on flat colour blocks where a normal hairline would do.
usedBy: shadcn/ui documentation site ("border-ghost" utility)
recipes.source: shadcn-ui apps/v4/app/globals.css ("@utility border-ghost": after:border after:mix-blend-darken dark:after:mix-blend-lighten)
recipes.pitfalls: mix-blend-mode creates a stacking context and can be costly on very large images. The source switches blend mode by theme class; this version uses two pseudo-elements so it follows color-scheme. For a simpler rule see image-outline-alpha.

recipes.name: Full-bleed section rules
recipes.looksLike: Thin horizontal lines that run past the content column to both edges of the window, so sections look ruled on a drafting grid.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: Content sits in a fixed column and the lines tie hero, features and footer into one measured grid.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: Lines are drawn around everything, including small cards, until the page looks like a spreadsheet.
usedBy: tailwindcss.com (line-t, line-b, line-y utilities and GridContainer)
recipes.source: tailwindcss-com src/app/globals.css and src/components/grid-container.tsx (technique only: pseudo-element rules wider than the container, 5% black in light and 10% white in dark)
recipes.pitfalls: 100vw includes the scrollbar, so clip horizontal overflow on body. The source is not open source; only the idea is used here. Decorative rules must stay at hairline contrast or they compete with real dividers.

recipes.name: Border beam (light travelling along the edge)
recipes.looksLike: A short streak of accent light that travels once around the border of a card.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: It marks one live or in-progress element (a running job, a recording, an AI reply being written) and stops when the state ends.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It loops forever on static marketing cards, or several beams run on one screen.

usedBy: Magic UI BorderBeam
Motion Primitives BorderTrail
cmdk website Raycast theme (one-shot border shine on open, 3s)
recipes.source: magicui apps/www/registry/magicui/border-beam.tsx (offsetPath "rect(0 auto auto 0 round Npx)", masked border ring, 6s linear); motion-primitives components/core/border-trail.tsx; cmdk website/styles/cmdk/raycast.scss ("animation: shine 3s ease forwards"); bcd css/properties/offset-path.json
recipes.pitfalls: offset-path with rect() needs Chrome 116, Firefox 122, Safari 18. The sources drive the motion with a JavaScript animation library; this version uses a CSS keyframe. Always pair the beam with a text or icon status, because motion alone is not a status signal.

recipes.name: Six-step elevation scale (ring + contact + ambient)
recipes.looksLike: Six shadow levels from a recessed well to a modal, each keeping a 1px ring so the edge stays sharp while the blur grows.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: The whole product uses the same scale: level 2 for resting cards, 3 for hover and menus, 5 for popovers, 6 for dialogs.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: Components pick shadows at random, or the largest level is used on resting cards.
usedBy: Radix Themes (--shadow-1 to --shadow-6; Dialog uses --shadow-6, classic Card uses --shadow-2)
recipes.source: radix-themes src/styles/tokens/shadow.css (light and dark sets), alpha values resolved from tokens.css; src/components/_internal/base-dialog.css (box-shadow: var(--shadow-6))
recipes.pitfalls: Level 1 in the source has three light layers and four dark layers; here it is reduced to two. Level 3 uses different blur geometry in dark mode, so it carries two extra layers that are transparent in the other scheme. Large blurs (60px) on many elements cost paint time: reserve levels 5 and 6 for one or two surfaces at a time.

recipes.name: Hue-tinted shadows with one strength knob
recipes.looksLike: Soft stacked shadows whose colour leans toward the page hue instead of pure black, with a single percentage that makes the whole set lighter or heavier.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: The page background is tinted (warm paper, cool slate, brand colour) and the shadow hue follows it.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: Pure black shadows sit on a coloured background and look like grey dirt, or the tint is so saturated it looks like a coloured glow.
usedBy: Open Props (--shadow-1 to --shadow-6, --shadow-color, --shadow-strength)
GUI Challenges buttons (same private shadow variables)
recipes.source: open-props src/props.shadows.css (--shadow-color "220 3% 15%", dark "220 40% 2%", --shadow-strength 1% and 25%, layer geometry verbatim); gui-challenges buttons/buttons.css; vercel-wig README.md ("Hue consistency")
recipes.pitfalls: The source switches the two knobs in a dark media query; this version keeps separate light and dark knobs so it follows color-scheme. Level 3 includes a small upward layer (0 -1px 3px) that brightens nothing but softens the top edge; drop it if the element sits under a sticky header.

recipes.name: Floating panel shadow (six smooth layers + ring)
recipes.looksLike: A menu or popover that seems to hover: the shadow falls off smoothly with no visible band, and a 1px ring keeps the edge defined.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: It is reserved for things that really float: dropdowns, popovers, command menus, toasts.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It is put on in-flow cards, making a dashboard look like a pile of loose paper.
usedBy: Supabase dashboard and website (floating-surface-shadow-sm and -md utilities)
recipes.source: supabase packages/config/css/shadows.css (layer geometry verbatim; the source multiplies every alpha by --floating-shadow-strength, 1 in light and 5 in dark, and switches the ring from black 5% to white 18%)
recipes.pitfalls: Seven layers on a large element are expensive to repaint while it animates: animate opacity and transform only, never the shadow. In dark mode the white ring does most of the work; without it the panel merges with the page.

recipes.name: Coloured shadow under accent elements
recipes.looksLike: A primary button whose shadow is a soft pool of its own colour rather than grey.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: Only the single primary action on a view carries it, at a quarter to under half strength, on a neutral background.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: Every button, badge and card glows in neon, or the glow is wider than the element it belongs to.
usedBy: HeroUI Button variant="shadow" ("shadow-lg shadow-primary/40")
coss ui / Cal.com design system default Button ("shadow-primary/24 shadow-xs", removed when pressed)
recipes.source: heroui dist/components/button.js (shadow variant: "shadow-lg shadow-primary/40"); coss-ui apps/ui/registry/default/ui/button.tsx ("shadow-primary/24 shadow-xs ... [:disabled,:active,[data-pressed]]:shadow-none"); tailwindcss theme.css (--shadow-xs, --shadow-lg geometry)
recipes.pitfalls: On dark backgrounds a coloured shadow turns into a visible glow, which is a different effect: reduce it to 20% or drop it. color-mix() needs Chrome 111, Firefox 113, Safari 16.2. A neutral (black or white) primary button gains nothing from this; use the lit-edge recipe instead.

recipes.name: Dark-mode card: inner highlight, hard ring, doubling shadows
recipes.looksLike: In dark mode, a card with a faint light line inside its top edge, a black seam around it and four short shadows that double in size; in light mode, a plain ring and two soft layers.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: Dark surfaces need separation without raising their brightness, for example cards on a near-black dashboard.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: Light-mode shadows are reused unchanged in dark mode, where they are invisible, and a bright border is added to compensate.
usedBy: Cult UI MinimalCard
recipes.source: cult-ui apps/www/registry/default/ui/minimal-card.tsx (light: "rgba(17,24,28,0.08) 0 0 0 1px, ... 0 1px 2px -1px, rgba(17,24,28,0.04) 0 2px 4px"; dark: inset highlights plus 2/4/8px doubling layers at 10% black)
recipes.pitfalls: The light ink rgb(17 24 28) is slightly blue; change it if the neutral palette is warm. Eight layers are fine for cards but too many for long lists: use shadow-as-border-ring for rows.

recipes.name: Bento card: quiet light shadow, under-lit dark surface
recipes.looksLike: In light mode a card with a barely visible ring and a wide, weak shadow; in dark mode a card with a soft white glow rising inside from its bottom edge.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: Large feature tiles need to feel like panels of one surface, not separate objects.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: The dark inner glow is coloured or strong enough to read as a neon tube.
usedBy: Magic UI BentoCard
recipes.source: magicui apps/www/registry/magicui/bento-grid.tsx ("[box-shadow:0_0_0_1px_rgba(0,0,0,.03),0_2px_4px_rgba(0,0,0,.05),0_12px_24px_rgba(0,0,0,.05)]", dark "[box-shadow:0_-20px_80px_-20px_#ffffff1f_inset]" and "[border:1px_solid_rgba(255,255,255,.1)]")
recipes.pitfalls: The dark glow needs a card at least about 160px tall; on small cards it fills the whole surface and washes out text. Check text contrast near the bottom edge in dark mode.

recipes.name: Shadow that follows a shape (drop-shadow filter)
recipes.looksLike: A tooltip with an arrow, or a cut-out image, whose shadow follows the real outline instead of the bounding box.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: The element is not a rectangle: tooltip with pointer, speech bubble, masked shape, transparent PNG or SVG.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It replaces box-shadow on ordinary rectangles, where it is slower and has no spread control.
usedBy: GUI Challenges tooltip (Adam Argyle)
recipes.source: gui-challenges tooltips/tool-tip.css ("filter: drop-shadow(0 3px 3px hsl(0 0% 0% / var(--_shadow-alpha))) drop-shadow(0 12px 12px ...)", alpha 15% light and 50% dark); tailwindcss theme.css (--drop-shadow-* scale for comparison)
recipes.pitfalls: filter creates a stacking context and a containing block for fixed children. drop-shadow has no spread or inset. Do not animate it; the source sets will-change: filter because of that cost.

recipes.name: Flat solid button with full state set

recipes.readsPremiumWhen: Every state is distinct and quick (150ms), and the disabled state turns neutral instead of becoming a washed-out version of the brand colour.

recipes.name: Radial spotlight glow
recipes.looksLike: A soft pool of light behind the top of a section, as if a lamp above the page were pointed at the headline.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: It is neutral (white on dark, or the accent at under 20%) and wide, so it lifts the headline area without a visible edge.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It is a saturated violet or blue-to-pink blob on a dark page, the default look of generated SaaS heroes.

Large low-alpha gradients band on 8-bit displays; a 3% to 5% grain overlay hides the bands. The source gradient is tuned for a near-black page; the 5% grey used in light mode is an addition.

recipes.name: Aurora mesh in OKLCH (restrained)
recipes.looksLike: Three very soft colour clouds behind a section, in neighbouring hues of equal brightness, at about 20% strength in light mode and 12% in dark.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: Hues stay within about 100 degrees of each other, lightness and chroma are equal so no cloud dominates, and the mesh sits behind one focal object.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It mixes far-apart hues (purple, pink, orange, cyan) at high strength across the full page, or animates. That is the stock gradient look of generated sites.
usedBy: cmdk website (seven radial gradients under "filter: blur(100px) saturate(150%)", opacity 0.2 in light and 0.1 in dark)

recipes.pitfalls: A blur filter on a large box is expensive on first paint and very expensive if anything inside animates: keep it static, and drop the filter on low-power targets (the gradients are already soft). oklch() needs Chrome 111, Firefox 113, Safari 15.4. Text over the mesh has no fixed contrast; keep text on a solid surface or test both extremes.

recipes.name: Noise grain overlay (inline SVG turbulence)
recipes.looksLike: A barely visible film grain over a section or gradient, like paper tooth or photographic noise.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: It is 3% to 6% strong, greyscale, and laid over gradients or large flat colour fields to hide banding and add material.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It is strong enough to see at a glance, coloured, animated, or laid over text and UI controls so they look dirty.
usedBy: Open Props (--noise-1 to --noise-5: inline SVG feTurbulence data URIs with stitchTiles)

recipes.pitfalls: The browser rasterises the SVG filter once per tile size, so keep the tile small (200px) and never animate it. Grain over text lowers legibility: the rule above lifts direct children over it. On high-density screens the grain looks finer; raise opacity to about 0.07 rather than scaling the tile.

recipes.name: Gradient fade dividers
recipes.looksLike: A hairline that is solid in the middle and fades to nothing at both ends, horizontal or vertical; and a 1px highlight along the top of a dark panel that is brightest off-centre.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: It separates regions that have no box around them (a sidebar from content, a header from a hero) so the line does not crash into the edges.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: The fading line is brand-coloured and glowing, or used between every list item where a plain border belongs.
usedBy: shadcn/ui documentation sidebar (1px rule: linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent 0%, border 10%, border 90%, transparent 100%))

recipes.pitfalls: A fading rule has no accessible meaning; use a real hr or border where the separation matters to structure, and give decorative ones role="presentation". In forced-colours mode background gradients are removed, so these lines vanish; that is acceptable only for decoration.

recipes.name: Vignette that fades a pattern into the page
recipes.looksLike: A background pattern or image that is clear in the centre and dissolves into the page colour toward every edge.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: It finishes a grid, dot field or screenshot so there is no visible rectangle where the decoration stops.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: It darkens the corners of ordinary content like an old photo filter.

recipes.name: Blurred glow behind a product frame
recipes.looksLike: A product screenshot or sign-in card with a soft band of brand colour behind it, smaller than the frame and blurred until it has no edge.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: It backs exactly one object, uses the brand colour and one close neighbour, and is smaller than the object so only a rim of light shows.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: The glow is larger than the frame, cycles through rainbow hues or rotates continuously.

recipes.name: Mask fades for edges of strips and illustrations
recipes.looksLike: A logo strip, marquee or illustration whose left and right ends (and optionally the bottom) fade out instead of being cut off.

recipes.readsClicheWhen: Fades are so wide that half the content is always dimmed.

recipes.readsClicheWhen: The gradient runs between two bright hues, appears on every heading, or is used on small text where it just looks faded.

recipes.readsClicheWhen: Headings wrap wherever the container happens to end, leaving one word alone on the second line of a hero.

recipes.name: Inter: OpenType features worth switching on
recipes.looksLike: Inter with small character changes: a single-storey a, open 4, 6 and 9, a slashed zero in data, straighter punctuation in capitals.

recipes.readsClicheWhen: Default Inter with no thought given to it, or a different feature mix on every component.

recipes.looksLike: The same typeface with sturdier, wider-spaced letters at caption sizes and finer, tighter letters at headline sizes.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: A font with an optical-size axis is used and left on automatic, so small text stays sturdy and large text stays fine with no extra rules.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: A font-variation-settings rule that sets weight also pins the optical size to one value, so headlines look clumsy or captions look spindly.

The hand-compensation weights need a variable font; static files only offer the named weights.

recipes.name: Tabular numerals and slashed zero
recipes.looksLike: Digits that all take the same width, so columns line up and counters do not wobble; optionally a zero with a slash so it cannot be read as the letter O.
recipes.readsPremiumWhen: Every number that updates or sits in a column uses tabular figures, and identifiers use a slashed zero.
recipes.readsClicheWhen: Prices jitter sideways as they change, table columns have ragged right edges, or tabular figures are forced onto large decorative statistics where proportional figures look better.
